summary: Medawachchiye Dhammajothi studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (BA, ~1990–1994), Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (MA, ~1995–1997), and Nanjing University (PhD, ~1998–2003). Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, he taught at the University of Colombo from around 2003.
Medhani is a scholar who pursued studies under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Megan Bryson, a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, completed her education at Stanford University. By 2017, she held an attested academic appointment at the University of Tennessee.

Megumu Honda (1931–2011) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Johannes Rahder (1961–1962), Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells. He served as a professor at Doho University, attested in 1996.

Mei Ching Hsuan works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Peter Schwieger and also taught by Dieter Schuh, she earned her PhD at the University of Bonn. By 2026, she was attested as a professor at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Meiji Yamada, a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He later served there as a professor, attested from 1963 to 1971 and again in 2007.

Meinrad Scheller (1921–1991) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch at the University of Zurich (Dr. phil., Habilitation), and also attended the University of Paris. He was a professor at Fribourg, Munich, and Zurich.
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.
Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar in history and archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Her doctoral studies were supervised by Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

Melvyn C. Goldstein (born 1938) is a Tibetologist and historian. He earned his BA at the University of Michigan (~1955–1959) and his PhD at the University of Washington (~1960–1968), later serving as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

Merab Mamardashvili (1930–1990) was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Mervin Viggo Hanson, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, having also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.
Mery Cecconi is an Indology scholar attested as a PhD candidate at Leiden University in 2026, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram (born 1956), a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, earned his doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He held long-term leadership positions at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Michael Aris (1946–1999) was a scholar in Tibetology and history who earned his BA at Durham and PhD at SOAS under David Snellgrove. He held appointments at Oxford (including St Antony's and Wolfson) and Harvard, and co-founded the International Association for Tibetan Studies.
Michael Balk worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Royal Library of Berlin, attested in 1991.

Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) studied at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. A specialist in art history, he served at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, the Courtauld Institute of Art, Oxford (Slade Professor 1974–1975), and the University of California, Berkeley.

Michael Bernays (1834–1897) studied at the University of Bonn and Heidelberg University, where he was taught by Adolf Holtzmann. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).
Michael C. Shapiro (born 1946) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Washington from ~1974 to 2013, becoming Professor Emeritus of Hindi around 2013.
